title: Weekday Mini Trackbook - latency & cost runs
content:
Purpose: quick weekday tracker for short bench runs + notes. Use this as a lightweight single-file reference before I move anything to /engineering or open a ticket.

Quick legend:
- ID: short run id (date + N)
- Model: variant used (fp16/8bit/qat)
- Seq: typical sequence length for this run (tokens)
- Batch: batch size
- AvgLat(ms): median 50p-95p bucket, rough single-request latency in ms
- Cost/1k: rough $ per 1k tokens (estimate from billing + run profile)
- Notes: quick observations, anomalies, follow-ups

Table (most recent at top):
ID	Date	Model	Seq	Batch	Tokens/req	AvgLat(ms)	Cost/1k	Outcome	Notes
20241114-1	2024-11-14	redwood-v2-small-q4	512	4	600	92	0.045	ok	prefix cache warmed; KV hit ~60% after 3rd request; spikes @95p ~180ms
20241113-a	2024-11-13	redwood-v2-small-fp16	256	8	300	68	0.062	ok	cheaper but tail slightly worse, consider bumping batch->6 to test latency/cost trade
20241030-x	2024-10-30	community-7b-8bit	1024	2	1100	155	0.028	review	quant artifacts on long sequences; hallucination check failed for prompt set B
20240618-3	2024-06-18	redwood-v1-medium-fp16	128	16	140	48	0.12	opti	good throughput, useful baseline for tiny prompt flows

Quick calcs / heuristics I use here:
- cost_per_1k ~= (billing_unit_token_cost_estimate) * (1) — I eyeball from calls and previous invoices, not precise.
- expected_latency ~= base_latency + (seq / 64)*per_64_token_cost + batch_penalty
- target: keep p50 < 80ms for interactive flows; allow p95 < 200ms.

Short todo / follow-ups:
- [ ] Re-run 20241114-1 with batch=2 to compare p95 tail (ticket: JIRA-INF-345?)
- [ ] Add a tiny prompt sweep: short vs long prefix to measure prefix cache benefits (need script to warm cache reliably)
- [ ] Compare redwood-v2-small-q4 vs community-7b-8bit on the same dataset, focus on hallucination Delta
- [ ] Capture CPU/GPU util metrics alongside (right now only have latency + cost) — ask SRE for quick capture command

Scratch notes / heuristics (messy):
- Warmed KV cache shows ~30-50% token saving for multi-turn; important for chat.
- Batching helps throughput but often increases median by 10-20ms; use adaptive batching for interactive endpoints.
- Quant artifacts at seq>900 are real for community variants; need a short eval set to catch them early.

Example quick command I ran (for my memory):
- ./local-run-bench --model redwood-v2-small-q4 --batch 4 --seq 512 --iters 250 --warmup 50 --log tail,p50,p95,cost

Notes to self about moving this to official repo:
- If results are repeatable, open PR to add 2 quick tests under infra/benchmarks/smoke (include config JSON).
- Keep this doc for at least 2 weeks after PR so I can paste raw runs as evidence in code review.

Random thoughts:
- Weekend idea: small script that auto-aggregates runs and outputs a weekly CSV so I can drop into the console for the week summary. Might be overkill but useful for recurring experiments.
- Check with Maya about shared runs — she had a different script that flattens latencies per backend (was in #bench-runs channel)

End of file (handy snapshot of my weekday quick-run thinking).
